title: Live Swarm Snapshot Compiler + Allocator Bridge V1
mission: Build a deterministic pinned-head read-only snapshot that compiles the live universal-worker state from active queues, claims, runs, returns, recovery evidence and proposal pins, then expose that snapshot as an allocator/control-room input so workers do not have to rediscover saturated lanes through long serial collision probing. Reuse the existing Control Room, allocator, stale scan and dynamic-readiness mechanisms; do not create a second authority plane.

unblock_value.reason: The throughput critic identified live snapshot/allocator wiring as a route-changing gap; workers currently reconstruct the same volatile state independently.

human_friction_reduction.reason: A durable live snapshot is a prerequisite for deriving useful free-worker demand and avoiding the human acting as scheduler/stale detector.

reuse_value.reason: The work should bind existing Control Room, allocator, readiness and stale-scan mechanisms rather than add another parallel subsystem.

must_fail_if: the same pinned repository head yields different logical snapshot output
RETURN without matching DONE is treated as dependency-satisfied
a stale suspicion is promoted to failure or takeover authority
the snapshot mutates queues/claims/runs/returns or becomes an authority source
allocator-visible READY/free slots diverge from exact source evidence without an explicit contradiction/block state
proof_required: allocator consumption test that preserves create-if-absent as final claim authority

acceptance_details: one pinned-head scan deterministically classifies prepared READY, claimed, STARTED, returned, done, stale-suspect, recovery-active and blocked-derived lanes
existing Control Room and allocator consume or can consume the snapshot without duplicating truth laws
snapshot output includes source head and exact source receipts and is idempotent on identical input
create-if-absent/CAS remains final ownership authority; snapshot is advisory/derived only
live canary demonstrates fewer redundant lane probes or a measurable equivalent reduction in allocation work
